findings.note: Hedman was healthy and active on Oct. 15, scoring the overtime winner against Seattle. It was his first goal since Feb. 28, and his coach said it should build his confidence after a long road back.

In the Oct. 1 opener's projected lineup, Hedman was on the second pair with Charle-Edouard D'Astous, behind McDonagh-Cernak. That could mean less ice time or power-play work than in his peak years. This is old lineup info and wasn't confirmed for Oct. 20.

Hedman returned Oct. 1 after missing the end of last season and the playoffs for mental health, plus earlier elbow surgery. He is nearly 36 and dropped weight to adjust to aging, so how well he'll hold up and produce is still unclear.
